Cujus mortem cùm filius Haiio ulcisceretur acerbiùs, ipsis crudelitatem improbantibus Monasteriensibus exorati à plebe Groningani, & propriis injuriis quoque lacessiti corrptis armis ejus arcem Weddanam in potestatem redactam æquarunt solo. Prætorium imperium, quod Haiionis fuerat, sibi sumpsêre summa plebis voluntate, præfectum, qui jurisdictioni præesset, in arce Pekelborgia recèns à se structa collocarunt. Et ne Monasteriensés offenderent, solutis xxv auri Rhenani libris eos deliniverunt, & jus, quod hactenus Eggo & Haiio velut beneficio eorum illic tenuerant, redemerunt. Additaque pecuniæ datæ conditio, uti tantisper in possessione potestatis hujusce manēret civitas, donec pecunia ei esset restituta. Hoc modo ex fœderatis Westerwoldiorum Rectores facti Groningani sunt, clientelam præsulis Monasteriensis professi: duraruntque in eo ad initia usque Saxonici Belli, quo cuncta in Frisia turbata. Quo eodem tempore id quod inter Houwerdæos & civitatem reliquum controversiæ erat, agitatum rursum, & arbitris demùm commissum. Per eos confecta res quoquo modo primùm inter Mennonem Omconemque fratres, & civitatem : deinde post aliquot annos etiam inter Ailconem & Gerlachum Ulphusanos , priorum fratris filios , ac eandem civitatem. Prioribus nescio qua re, posterioribus pecunia non ampla satisfactum : jurisdictio ab utrisque civitati relicta. Sed redeo ad ea , unde sum, prolixius quam constitueram, digressus. Finitis fœderibus ante memoratis , quæ cum reliquo agro inter Lavicam & Ama-sum civitas habebat, usus tamen eorum prorogatus tacito partium consensu , annoque M. cccc. Lv. etiam de frumenti exportatione & cerevisia scripto repetitum, & sancitum diligentius , ut in antigrapho quodam , quod apud ipsos agrarios est , legi. Demùm , cùm pessum ire non-nulla, nulla, & diffluere sensim viderentur, & motus à Carolo Burgundo ingrueret Frisiæ minitante, optimi & prudentissimi quique Reip. & patriæ totius cura tacti id effecere studio suo, ut prolixius accuratiusque quàm unquam priùs civitati cum Fivelgoniis, Hunesgoniis, Medachiis, Langowoldiis, Fredowoldiis, Hummerziis solenni modo fœdus sit instauratum, cùm flueret annus à natali Servatoris nostri M. CCCC. LXXIII. In eo hæc fuere præcipua: Vt pacatè inter se viverent omnes, auxilio sibi mutuò essent contra quoslibet hostes, maximè libertati imminentes, contraque eos, qui domi judiciis & legibus non parerent: vis omnis & tumultus statim comprimeretur; conventus juridici superiores Groningæ agerentur quater quotannis aut sæpius, quibus Hovetmanni oppidani præsiderent, ad quos provocatio esset à tribunalibus omnibus in agro. Conventus hos Hovetmanni cum judicibus aliis indicerent: quod frumenti in agro provenit, id non exportaretur, nec alibi quàm in urbe venum proponeretur: in tabernis & diversoriis non alius quàm Groninganæ cervisiæ esset usus: nec cuiquam per totum agrum vendendi, ac quæstus faciendi causâ cerevisiam coquere liceret: fœdus hoc decennium proximum valeret. Signatum die vi Augusti. Eodem anno, crescente, quem dixi, ab armis Burgundicis metu, cùm fœdus cum Translavicanis confici ob simultates atque odia intestina non posset, cum Theda & Frisiis orientalibus societas à civitate ordinibusque agrariis inita est pro tuendâ libertate certè memorabilis: de quâ in Historiâ scripsi plenius. Mox alio se vertente Burgundo, legati à civitate & sociis vicinis missi ad Cæsarem Fridericum III, qui & libertatis pristinæ, & pactorum recentium confirmationem, patrociniumque contra Burgundum peterent: Im-petratumq; de libertate, pactaq; firmata, tota regio denique in tutelam recepta Imperii. Sed ex eâ legatione non magnam gratiam, honorémve Ioannes Rengerus & Unico Ripperda retulêre, qui pro Rep. missi sua potiùs quàm reip. agentes, potestatem peramplam juris dicundi, exigendi vectigalis, cudendæ aureæ monetæ (hanc civitas pro se petierat) & nescio quæ alia sibi acquisivêre : quamquam prohibiti ab Ordinibus patriæ uti beneficio Cæsaris non potuerunt. Simul tota regio durante hoc fœdere in summâ quiete & felicitate egit, civitas divitiis, operibus novis, magnificentiâ, amplitudine, ager cultu & nitore crevit, ac fuit summa inter socios animorum & gerendæ Reip. conjunctio. Hoc tempore, cæso jam ad Nanceium Carolo Burgundo, Arnoldus Lous Iureconsultus, à Cæsare Friderico ad componendas res per Frisiam Translavicanam missus,consilii capiendi causâ Groningam deflexit. Eo autore civitas in spem venit perpetuæ potestatis jus in agrum vicinum sibi parandi : paravissetque, & alia quoque adjecisset, quantum in Cæsare erat, si pecuniæ dispendium in loco facere voluisset. Rediit enim Lous denuò à Cæsare, amplissimis in hanc rem mandatis instructus. Sed illa aulæ cupidine offensa,postposito consilio hoc, inanem legatum remisit. Et jam ad exitum penè properabat tempus, quod erat fœderi dictum, ut aut prorogato eodem, aut novato ampliatóve opus esse videretur. Gaudebat quippe utraque pars fœdere, ejusque fructu suaviter afficiebatur. Itaque data utrimque opera est, ut ampliatum rebus & tempore denuò feriretur. Idque confectum exeunte anno M. CCCC. LXXXII, triduò ante natalem Domini: tempus ei decretum superiore majus. Ejus capita præcipua fuére hæc, ut sunt in Historiâ à me expressa: Pax inter partes esset, salvo cuique legitimo jure suo; auxiliis se mutuò juvarent, si res auxiliis egeret; temerè nemo in exilium pelleretur, nisi criminum gravium reus, & contumax: ex legibus sese mutuò convenirent, omni vi missâ: Principes externos, & quoscunque alios vim sociis asserentes, aut libertatem prementes communi operâ pro viribus arcerent: postulati auxilia ferrent ad arbitrium bonorum virorum, & statim, & suis sumptibus; cessantesq; in hoc officio ꝓM[?]. scutatos veteres in usum apparatus bellici penderent: tumultuantes comprimerentur maturè: si qui turbatâ pace publicâ ceperint alios, ac spoliarint, captos dimitterent confestim, spolioque duplicitèr restituto insuper gravem multam fœderi sverent[?]: sine consensu communi bellum nemo moveret: in auxilium evocati à sociis fidei firmandæ causâ obsidesque traderent Groningæ custodiendos usque ad expeditionis finem.
units.tr: It was expressly provided that if the judges of the Territory (there were twelve of them, chosen by the people and from among the people) were thought to have judged unjustly, the injured party might appeal to the senate of Groningen within ten days; the senate would have the right to summon the judges and re-examine the case, and, if the appellant was found to have brought a frivolous appeal, or the judges to have judged unjustly, to condemn them to five old marks. All this was to be without prejudice to the right of Eggo and of the whole people, and to the liberty received from their ancestors, so far as it did not conflict with the articles of this covenant. The covenant was to be perpetual. It was signed the day before the feast of Bartholomew. From this time the city was accustomed to live under that covenant, and through fear of it Eggo dared to behave less arrogantly; until at last, casting off fear and despising the covenant, and now advanced in years, he grew more insolent through the confidence of his Münster patrons and was killed by the enraged commons. When his son Haiio avenged his death more savagely, the Münster men disapproved of the cruelty, and the Groningen commons, having been petitioned and also provoked by their own injuries, took up arms and levelled to the ground the castle of Weddan, which had been brought under their control. They took on for themselves the praetorian authority that had belonged to Haiio, with the full will of the commons, and placed a prefect, to preside over jurisdiction, in the castle of Pekelborg, recently built by themselves. And so that they would not offend the Münster men, they soothed them by paying twenty-five pounds of Rhenish gold, and bought back the right which Eggo and Haiio had hitherto held there as a favour from them. And a condition was added to the payment: that the city should remain in possession of this power for the time being, until the money was repaid to them. In this way the rulers of the Westerwolde allies became the Groningen men, professing the clientage of the Münster prelate; and they persisted in this until the beginning of the Saxon War, by which all of Friesland was thrown into confusion. At that same time, the dispute that remained between the Houwerda family and the city was stirred up again, and at last committed to arbitrators. Through them the matter was settled, somehow, first between the brothers Menno and Omcon and the city, and then, some years later, also between Ailco and Gerlach of Ulfsund, sons of the elder brother, and the same city. The former were satisfied by I know not what means, the latter by no large sum of money; the jurisdiction was left to the city by both. But I return to my subject, having digressed at greater length than I had intended. When the aforementioned covenants that the city had with the rest of the land between Lauwers and Ems were concluded, their use was nevertheless extended by the tacit consent of the parties, and in the year 1455 the export of grain and beer was also regulated again in writing, and confirmed more carefully, as can be read in a certain copy that is kept among the landholders themselves. At last, when some things seemed to be going to ruin, some were nothing, and everything was gradually dissolving, and the movement of Charles of Burgundy threatened Friesland, the best and wisest men, moved by concern for the commonwealth and the whole fatherland, took care with their zeal that a covenant should be solemnly renewed between the city and the Fivelgo, Hunsingo, Medemblik, Langewold, Fredewold and Hummerzijl, more lengthily and carefully than ever before, in the year that ran from the birth of our Saviour 1473. Its chief points were these: that all should live peaceably among themselves, should help one another mutually against any enemies, especially those threatening liberty, and against those who would not obey judgments and laws at home; every violence and tumult should be checked at once; the higher court sessions should be held at Groningen four times a year or more often, presided over by the town hetmen, to which appeal should lie from all tribunals in the countryside. The hetmen of the town, with other judges, were to call these sessions: that the grain grown in the countryside should not be exported, and should be offered for sale only in the city; that in taverns and inns only Groningen beer should be used; and that no one throughout the whole countryside should be allowed to brew beer for sale and to make a profit; this covenant was to hold for the next ten years. It was signed on the sixth day of August. In the same year, with the fear of the Burgundian arms growing, as I have said, and since a covenant could not be made with the Trans-Lauwers districts because of their internal quarrels and hatreds, an alliance was entered into by the city and the landholding orders with Thedinga and the eastern Frisians for the defence of liberty, certainly a memorable one, which I have described more fully in my History. Soon afterwards, when Burgundy turned elsewhere, envoys were sent by the city and its neighbouring allies to Emperor Frederick III, to seek confirmation of their former liberty and of the recent pacts, and protection against Burgundy: liberty was obtained, the pacts were confirmed, and the whole region was at last taken under the protection of the Empire. But from this embassy John Rengers and Unico Ripperda brought back no great favour or honour, for they, sent on behalf of the commonwealth, pursued their own interests rather than those of the commonwealth, and acquired for themselves a very ample power of administering justice, of collecting tolls, of minting gold coin (the city had asked for this for itself), and I know not what else; although, forbidden by the orders of the fatherland, they could not use the emperor's favour. At the same time, while this covenant lasted, the whole region lived in the greatest peace and prosperity: the city grew in riches, new buildings, magnificence and size, and the countryside in cultivation and splendour, and there was the greatest unity of minds among the allies and in the conduct of public affairs. At this time, Charles of Burgundy having now been slain at Nancy, Arnold Lous, a jurist sent by Emperor Frederick to settle affairs throughout Trans-Lauwers Friesland, turned aside to Groningen to take counsel. Through his advice the city came to hope for a perpetual right to acquire power over the neighbouring countryside; and it would have acquired it, and more besides, as far as lay with the emperor, had it been willing to bear the expense at the place. For Lous returned again from the emperor, furnished with very ample instructions for this business. But the court, offended by this eagerness, set aside this plan and sent the envoy back empty-handed. And now the time fixed in the covenant was almost running out, so that it seemed necessary either to extend the same, or to renew it and enlarge it. For both parties rejoiced in the covenant and were pleasantly affected by its fruits. Accordingly, efforts were made on both sides that it should be struck anew, enlarged in its matters and in its term. And this was done at the end of the year 1482, three days before the birth of the Lord: its term was fixed longer than the former one. Its chief points were these, as I have set them out in my History: that there should be peace between the parties, each keeping his lawful right; that they should help each other with aid, if the matter needed aid; that no one should be thrust into exile rashly, except one guilty of grave crimes and contumacious; that they should meet by the laws, every violence set aside; that foreign princes and any others who threatened violence to the allies or oppressed liberty should be repelled by common effort, as far as their strength allowed; that those requested should bring aid at the judgment of good men, and at once, and at their own expense; and that those who were slack in this duty should pay into the use of the military preparations the old scutati, and that tumults should be quickly suppressed; that if anyone, having disturbed the public peace, had seized others and plundered them, he should release the captives immediately, and, the plunder having been restored twofold, should pay in addition a heavy fine to the covenant; that no one should begin war without common consent; and that those summoned to aid by the allies, for the sake of strengthening the faith, should hand over hostages to be kept at Groningen until the end of the expedition.

units.la: Tum de judiciis sic: Iudicibus in Agro aut jus reddere detrectantibus, aut perperam judicantibus, jus esset læso appellare tribunal superius, in quo judicant omnes totius societatis ordines legitimè convocati, ejusque appellationis testimonium scriptum petere Groningæ intra diem x. quo accepto, non liceret judici inferiori quicquam in eum porrò decernere, aut contra eum agere, aut repetenti pignora, si qua sint ablata, ac sponsionem præstare volenti in morâ aut impedimento esse: aut illum diem si negligeret læsus, omninò judicato priori pateret: appellans, causam suam persequeretur tribus proximis in conventibus judicialibus in ipsâ urbe, aut marcas penderet veteres quinque mulctæ nomine, insuperque causâ suâ caderet: atque hic esset litium trahendarum terminus, nec fas esset in hoc quicquam mutare, nisi ex mutuo litigantium partium consensu: judex inferior, à cujus judicio provocatum esset, si non veniret ipse tuendæ sententiæ suæ gratiâ ad conventum, primùm detrimento id non esset appellanti, deinde præter emansitationis pœnam usitatam, quinque etiam marcas fisco solveret: si latam ab eo sententiam confirmari contingeret, potestatem haberet totam causam porrò definiendi, etiamsi anno suo evoluto magistratu jam abiisset: ad conventum judicialem coeuntibus judicandi gratiâ quantumvis raro numero jus esset ac potestas causas definiendi, non secus ac si frequentes convenissent: Conventus hujusmodi Groningæ agerentur quotannis quater aut sæpius, si Reip. ratio id videretur poscere: esset-que in eo, ut & in tempore conventuum designando, arbitrium prætorum ab oppidanis datorum (Hovetmannos vocant) & eorum qui res per [?]Agrum in tribunalibus inferioribus judicant: Deinde de fontium pœnis aut mulctis hæc: Furti, latrocinii, proditionis, incendiorum reos receptare fas non esset, aut pœnis eripere: pœna omnium horum, supplicium capitis. Cædes cujusvis hominis in conventu publico præsentis, aut ìstuc euntis, aut redeuntis ab eo, mulctâ lueretur sexcuplâ: idem juris de vulnere, aliâve injuriâ esset: Consulis vero aut senatoris, aut viri nobilis, aut judicis, aut sacerdotis caedes, vulnus, injuria multâ corriperetur duodecuplâ: ejus multæ triens ærario, bes laeso, aut propinquis ejus cederet: si reus solvendo non esset, sex propinqui proximi laeso, aut laesi propinquis pro ipso satisfacerent, aut reum saltem iisdem sisterent: omnes denique in juria ubicunque & quocunque tempore patrata hoc durante foedere in triplum punirentur supra modum in legibus patriis definitum: salvo interea unicuique jure suo, ac pactis mutuis, quæ hisce non adversarentur. Demum & ista addita, quæ ad civitatis commodum pertinent: Frumenti in agro sociorum nati exportatio non esset in regiones alias: Cerevisiam in tabernis vendere, aut in usu habere exoticam totâ in regione non liceret, nisi quantum antistitibus aut nobilibus aut ceteris viris honestis condere ejus in penuaria suâ in usum domesticum liberet: nec coquere etiam toto in agro cerevisiam distrahendi causa, cuiquam extra urbem permissum: sed qui vellet, coqueret tantum, quantum satis esset familiæ suæ: veniret autem solum ea, quæ à civibus in urbe coctâ. Postremò, sub exitum fœderis utri parti conditio ejus displiceret, nec liberet eâ uti diutius, toto anno ante exitum ejus renunciaret eidem solenniter. Hoc fœdus quamdiu stetit & cultum sine vitio est, florentissimæ res Vrbis & Agri fuêre, adeò ut invidiam meruisse ex fortunâ videantur. Tum structa in urbe est turris illa maximi operis & impendii, vastæ molis & formæ superbæ ex saxo Benthemio,templo Martiniano adsidens; tum ædificatum magnificum cænopolium in fori medio; tum ædes privatæ complures sumptu ingenti erectæ; negotiationes etiam auctæ plurimùm, & opes publicæ privatæque multiplicatæ: denique hoc fortunæ rivo elata civitas, ut commeatuum haberet copiam liberiorem & ampliorem, re cum Episcopo Monasteriensi, Emdensium rebus inimico, comparatâ, Amasi alveum alio divertere, ut & in Dullarti sinus superiora, quâ ipsa imperium habet, derivare est conata, quamquam conatu frustraneo, & oleo operâque in eo perditâ: postremo trans Lavicam fidentius tentare res, & imperium proferre ausa fiat. De quo nunc dicere, & conjunctionem civitatis cum Translavicanis paulò altiùs repetere, ut res clariùs elucescat, ordo & tempus monent.
units.tr: Then, concerning judicial matters, the terms were as follows: If the judges in the Ommelands either refused to dispense justice or judged wrongly, the injured party had the right to appeal to a higher court, in which all the legitimately summoned orders of the whole alliance sit in judgment. He was to seek a written attestation of this appeal at Groningen within ten days. Once he had received it, the lower judge was not permitted to decree anything further against him, to act against him, or to stand in the way of the appellant who wished to recover pledges, if any had been taken, or to give security. If the injured party neglected that day, the earlier judgment would stand entirely. The appellant was to pursue his case over the three nearest judicial sessions held in the city itself; otherwise he would forfeit his case and pay five old marks as a fine. This was to be the limit of prolonging lawsuits, and it was not lawful to change it except by mutual consent of the litigating parties. If the lower judge, from whose decision the appeal had been made, did not come to the session in person to defend his own sentence, then, first, this would not be to the disadvantage of the appellant; and second, besides the customary penalty for absence, the judge would also pay five marks to the treasury. If the sentence he had pronounced were confirmed, he would have the power to settle the whole case afterwards, even if he had already left office after his year of magistracy had run out. When they met at a judicial session for the purpose of judging, however small their number, the judges had the right and power to decide cases, just as if they had met in full attendance. Such sessions were to be held at Groningen four times a year, or more often if the state of the commonwealth seemed to require it. The choice of the times for holding these sessions was to rest with the praetors chosen by the townsmen (they call them Hovetmannos) and with those who judge affairs in the lower tribunals throughout the Ommelands. Next, concerning penalties and fines for crimes, the following: It was not lawful to harbour the perpetrators of theft, robbery, treason or arson, or to snatch them from punishment. The penalty for all of these was capital punishment. The killing of any man present at a public session, or going to it or returning from it, was to be atoned for with a sixfold fine; the same law applied to wounding or other injury. But the killing, wounding or injury of a consul, senator, noble man, judge or priest was to be punished with a twelvefold fine: a third of this fine would go to the treasury, and the rest to the injured party or his relatives. If the culprit was unable to pay, six nearest relatives of the injured party, or of the injured party's kin, were to give surety on his behalf, or at least present the offender to them. Finally, all wrongs committed anywhere and at any time while this covenant lasted were to be punished threefold, beyond the measure defined in the native laws; meanwhile each person's right remained safe, along with mutual agreements that were not opposed to these terms. Lastly, these clauses were also added, which pertain to the advantage of the city: The export of grain grown in the territory of the allies to other regions was not permitted. It was not lawful to sell or keep foreign beer in taverns throughout the whole region, except that the bishops, nobles, and other respectable men might store as much of it in their own pantries as they wished for domestic use. Nor was anyone outside the city permitted to brew beer throughout the whole territory for the purpose of selling it; rather, whoever wished might brew only as much as would suffice for his own household, and only that beer brewed by citizens in the city might be sold. Finally, at the end of the covenant, if either party found its terms displeasing and did not wish to continue using them any longer, it was to renounce them formally to the other party a full year before the covenant expired. As long as this covenant stood and was kept without fault, the affairs of the city and the Ommelands flourished greatly, so much so that they seem to have drawn envy because of their prosperity. Then that famous tower of great labour and expense was built in the city, of vast bulk and proud form, made of Bentheim stone, standing beside the church of St. Martin; then a magnificent cloth hall was erected in the middle of the marketplace; then many private houses were raised at great cost; trade also increased greatly, and public and private wealth multiplied. Finally, the city, lifted up by this stream of fortune, and wishing to have a freer and ampler supply of provisions, having made an arrangement with the Bishop of Münster, an enemy of the Emden people, attempted to divert the channel of the Ems elsewhere, and also tried to lead its upper waters into the Dollard bay, where the city itself has jurisdiction; but this attempt came to nothing, and oil and labour were wasted on it. Last of all, it dared to attempt matters more boldly across the Lauwers and to extend its rule. Concerning this, and to trace the union of the city with the Translavicani somewhat further back, so that the matter may be made clearer, the order and the time require me now to speak.

units.la: DE CONJUNCTIONE CIVITATIS CUM TRAN- SLAVICANIS.
units.tr: CONCERNING THE UNION OF THE CITY WITH THE TRANS-LAVICANS.

units.la: IN Transflavicanis Octopagici, Cislavicanis finitimi, primi post Scirin-gios à Kenone Groningâ ejectos, commodo societatis cum civitate animadverso, iisdem conditionibus, quibus Hummerzii, Langowoldii, Fredowoldii in commune fœdus ascripti, eidem quoq; se potestati prætoriæ subjecere, & eadem, quæ indè profluunt commoda civitati tribuerunt, cùm annus flueret à nato Christo M. cccc. xvi: tempusque fœderi dederunt decennium. Deinde finito decennio, cùm utilitatem rei essent experti, metuerentque priora mala ἐςόροις[?] demptis, fœdus idem indefinitè, nullo statuto termino prorogarunt, additis etiam ad priores socios Hunesgoniis & Fivelgoniis, sed conventuum loco Adoardiæ constituto. Hinc post annos xviiij, anno scilicet M[?] cccc. xliv, Ost-broecsterani, Collumani, Suachii, Oldwoldii, Gastii pacti cum civitate Groninganâ sunt in hanc sententiam: Si judices ipsorum in coercendis maleficiis officium non facerent, jus esset senatui urbano, & Hovetmannis, mandare iis, ut facerent: Si netum quidem moveri se sinerent, citarentur ab iisdem GRONINGAM, ad conventum juridicum: & causa cognita, si cessasse in officio deprehenderentur, multam gravem poscerentur; & ad solvendam eam compellerentur. Nec multis interjectis diebus omnes Ostergoi, ut se domesticis turbis ac dissensionibus perpetuis liberarent, cum frustra id prius pactionibus inter se, & cum Westergois vicinis quæsissent propter factionum pertinaciam sæpè pacta perrumpentem, ad hujus ejusdem civitatis Gronin-gana societatem confugerunt, conventumque juridicum ad cognoscendas controversias majores, de quibus provocatum ab xviii-viris judicibus superioribus, curandaque negotia Reip. agendum semel quotannis Groningæ collocarunt. Ad hæc hæc statuerunt, ut in arbitriis rerum criminalium, si arbitri convenire non possent, senatus Groninganus summus arbiter fieret; atque interim reus obsides solvendi judicati eidem daret: ut item nobilis vir nobilem occidens, luendæ pœnæ CCCC marcarum veterum intra annum vertentem obsides Groningæ deponeret, atque insuper Groninganæ Keip. marcas similes XX, totidemque singulis Ostergoæ partibus pro multa penderet: eo facto, extra periculum esset: si non daret obsides, atque interea aliquid à propinquis occisi pateretur, id authoribus esset impune. Denique sic recepère, Ostergoi, operam daturos se conjunctis studiis, ut Westergoi quoque eidem fœderi, iisdem conditionibus accederent. Hoc fœdus valeret quadriennium.
units.tr: Among the Transflavicans, the Octopagians, neighbours of the Cislavicans, were the first after the Sciringians, who had been driven out of Groningen by Kenon, to notice the advantage of alliance with the city. On the same terms as the Hummerzians, Langwoldians and Fredewoldians, who had been enrolled in the common league, they also submitted themselves to the authority of the praetor and granted the city the same benefits that follow from it. This was in the year 1416 after the birth of Christ, and they gave the league a term of ten years. Then, when the ten years had ended, and having learned the usefulness of the arrangement, and fearing that the former troubles would return (though they had been removed), they extended the same league indefinitely, with no fixed end. The Hunsingoans and Fivelgoans were also added to the earlier allies, but the assembly was set at Ayardsveen. Then, after nineteen years, in the year 1444, the people of Oostbroek, Collum, Zuawe, Oldwolde and Gaast made a pact with the city of Groningen to this effect: "If their judges did not perform their duty in restraining crimes, the city senate and the Hovetmanni shall have the right to order them to do so. If they allowed the matter to stand unmoved, they shall be summoned by the same men to the judicial assembly at Groningen; and, once the case has been heard, if they are found to have failed in their duty, they shall be fined heavily and compelled to pay it." Within a few days, not many, all the Ostergoans, wishing to free themselves from their constant domestic disturbances and quarrels (which they had first tried in vain to settle among themselves and with their neighbours the Westergoans, since the obstinacy of the factions often broke their agreements), took refuge in the alliance of this same city of Groningen. They placed the judicial assembly at Groningen, to hear the greater disputes appealed from the eighteen-man judges of the higher courts, and to handle the business of the commonwealth once a year. They also decided that in arbitration of criminal cases, if the arbiters could not agree, the senate of Groningen should become the final arbiter; and meanwhile the accused should give hostages to the senate for payment of the judgment. Likewise, a nobleman who killed a nobleman was to deposit hostages at Groningen for payment of a penalty of 400 old marks within a year, and in addition pay as a fine twenty similar marks to the commonwealth of Groningen, and as many to each district of Ostergo. Once this was done, he would be out of danger. If he did not give hostages, and meanwhile the relatives of the dead man took some action against him, this would go unpunished, at the authority of the leaders. Finally, the Ostergoans undertook, with united efforts, to work so that the Westergoans too might join the same league on the same terms. This league was to last four years.

units.la: Sed prorogatum duravit diutius ad adventum usque Thomæ Guristedii legati Cæsaris, qui in Frisiam venit anno M. CCCC. LVI. &, ni me animus fallit, etiam ulterius. Nam eo tempore quæsita.
units.tr: But the extended term lasted longer, until the arrival of Thomas Guristedius, the emperor's envoy, who came to Friesland in the year 1456, and, if I am not mistaken, even further. For at that time the Ostergoans and Sciringians sought from the emperor the annulment of this agreement; but I do not find that it was expressly annulled in the diplomas then obtained.

units.la: apud Imperatorem antiquatio ejus est à Westergois & Sciringiis: at antiquatum esse nominatim in diplomatis tunc impetratis non invenio. Similiter verò & Smalingani anno, qui proximè pactionem hanc Ostergoorum secutus fuit, aliquid hujus generis cum iisdem oppidanis, & eorum sociis vicinis pepigêre. Imprimis hîc cautum, ut judiciales conventus ageréntur quotannis, indicente senatu Groningano: & si socii hi novisuo in agro conventum haberi cuperent, ut hoc senatui significarent: is porrò edicto suo socios convocaret. Anno deinceps M. cccc. LXI, Up-sterani, qui etiam sunt ad Occidentem Lavicæ amnis, eandem secuti causam, ut dissensionibus intestinis & periculis se eximerent, ad idem quoque remedium rursum convolarunt. Nam instaurata memoriâ & vi veteris fœderis, novum multis capitibus auctum cum senatu populoque Groningano percusserunt in perpetuum. In eo hæc sunt: Hovetmanni Groningani, adhibitis in consilium tribus aut quatuor Vpsteranis hominibus honestis, prætorem toti agro creanto quotannis die translationis S. Martini, & similiter judices binos in parochiis majoribus, singulos in minoribus ex ordine eorum omnes, qui propria prædia in agro Vpsterano possident: hi jus omnibus æqualiter dicunto ex legibus patriis. Si in eo negligent, aut facere non volent officium suum, Hovetmanni Groningani compellantor, iisque sub pœnâ primum scutatorum x, deinde xx, postremò contumaciæ mandanto, ut jus petentibus expediant: multaque huiusmodi ex semisse civitatis, reliquum Reip. Vpsteranæ esto. Electus prætor aut judex munus annuum non recusato, aut x scutatos Reip. pendito. Prætor judicesque sententiam à se latam petentibus scriptam exhibento.
units.tr: Likewise, in the year after the Ostergoans' agreement, the Smallingerlanders also made some agreement of this kind with the same townspeople and their neighbouring allies. Above all, it was provided here "that judicial assemblies should be held every year, summoned by the Groningen senate; and if these allies wished an assembly to be held in their own district, they were to signify this to the senate, which would then summon the allies by its own edict." In the year 1461 afterwards, the Upstalsboomers, who also live on the western side of the River Lauwers, following the same cause, flocked together again to the same remedy, so that they might free themselves from internal dissensions and dangers. For, renewing the memory and force of the old league, they struck a new covenant, enlarged with many articles, with the senate and people of Groningen, to last forever. In it the following are contained: "The Groningen Hovetmanni, taking into counsel three or four honest men of the Upstalsboomers, shall appoint each year a praetor for the whole district on the day of the translation of St Martin, and similarly two judges in the larger parishes and one each in the smaller, chosen in turn from all those who own property in the Upstalsboom district. These judges shall administer justice equally to all, according to the ancestral laws. If they neglect this, or are unwilling to perform their duty, the Groningen Hovetmanni shall compel them, first under a penalty of ten gold shields, then twenty, and finally they shall be handed over for contumacy, so that they may dispense justice to those who seek it; and fines of this kind shall go half to the city and the rest to the commonwealth of the Upstalsboomers. A praetor or judge who has been elected shall not refuse the yearly office, or else he shall pay ten shields to the commonwealth. The praetor and judges shall give to those seeking it a written copy of the sentence pronounced by them."

units.la: Ab hac appellandi jus esto, si quis volet, ad Hovetmannos Groninganos intra diem decimum.
units.tr: From this, a right of appeal shall exist, if anyone wishes, to the Groningen Hovetmanni within ten days.

units.la: Quo rite facto, prior judex non procedito longius: causa refertor ad conventum juredicialem proximum in urbe.
units.tr: When this has been duly done, the first judge shall not proceed any further; the case is to be referred to the next judicial assembly in the city.

units.la: Appellans verò si non persequetur litem in proximo, aut saltem altero conventu, non solum lite cadito, sed etiam marcas quinque multam solvito: nisi forte judex, qui sententiam tulit, ad conventum ipse non veniat: hoc enim appellantem à pœnâ absolvet, judex verò emansitans pœnam pendito. Idem judex & appellans quinas marcas deponunto apud conventum, amittitoque depositum, qui succumbet, victor recipito. Signatum foedus feriâ quartâ à Pentecostes anno M. CCCC. LXI. Sexennio post Collumani quoque eorumque vicini seditionibus agitati diu, ac miserè afflicti, nec aliud remedium ullum conspicati, multis & exquisitis precibus fatigarunt Groninganos, ut se in fœdus reciperent. Assensu impetrato, fœdus initum in annos xxx. Ejus hæc fuit sententia: Civitas & Collumani, cæterique inter se comparent de domo valida & idoneâ, in quâ, velut in arce, sedem habeat præfectus à civitate dandus in annos proximos VI. In hujus præfecti stipendium quotannis pecunia conferatur viritim per totum agrum, ab aliis scutatus aureus, ab aliis semissis, pensionibus duabus: Ipse auxilio sit omnibus contra vim ac injuriam: valla, fossas, cætera munitionum poscente præfecto populus perficiat: post sexennium civitas & socii dispiciant, præsidione diutius sit opus, & quod videbitur iis, id valeat: criminum judicia exerceantur ex legibus proximo sæculo Groningæ recognitis: nemo factionibus tumultibusve aliis etiam extra regionem se misceat, aut suos miscere se sinat: contra vim armatam socii sibi mutuò auxilio sint: Turbat.e pacis gravis multa sta fit aureorum scutatorum mille, aut pœna capitis, si quis multam solvere non queat: vis omnis absit, non armis, sed judicio controversiæ disceptentur, facinora severè reprimantur: æris alieni solutio expediatur: in controversiis civilibus appellatio sit adjudices urbanos, quemadmodum receptum apud alios, qui cum civitate fœdus habent: qui in legationem ad senatum non consensere per agrum Collumanum & vicinum, in quibus ij, qui sunt prius nominati, fœdere hoc non sint comprehensi: fœdus valeat in annos xxx. Signatum anno M.CCCC.LXVII postridiè Nonarum Septembr. Præfecti duo, quod id expedire in initio videretur, in agrum Collumanum missi, Hillebrandus Brandus, & Sibrandus Ulverdi. Ita quies ibi parta: anno postero domus præsecto structa. Post hæc, cùm dissidia & turbæ crebrescerent rursus in Oftergoâ, flammâque eâ Westergoa quoque afflaretur, scintillaretque passim odium factionum, & cum civitate Groningana multorum simultas ex invidiâ & metu glisceret, ne quid indè majoris exisseret mali, tandem anno M. cccc. lxxvii, prudentum & bonorum studio, omnis Westergoa & Ostergoa in fœdus decenne cum civitate Groninganâ consensit. Cujus Hæc summa: Id quod anno M. cccc. xxii, à totâ gente Frisicâ Groningæ initum fœdus fuit, ratum sit, salvo nupero fœdere Collumano: Groninganis non licet at hoc decennio ullam præterea Ostergoæ aut Westergoæ partem fœdere hujusmodi implicare, aut prætoriæ potestati suæ subjicere: Conventus quotannis agatur alternis vicibus Groningæ & Leoardiæ, ad quem quini ab utraque parte homines sapientes mittantur: hiis x undecimus adjiciatur, quem ex Ostergoâ aut Westergoâ quini Groningani eligent, cùm conventus agetur Leoardiæ: quini verò Transflavicani, ex oppido aut agro Groningano cùm conventus ille Groningæ habebitur. Horum arbitrii sit causas omnes publicas & privatas, quæ in controversiam venient, cognoscere, disceptare, definire: quicquid definiverint, ab omnibus ratum habeatur: intraque præfixum tempus executioni mandetur ab iis apud quos sedes tenet condemnatus, aut ab ipsis illis multa peta-tur: tur : contumaces, si qui erunt, conjunctis viribus ad parendum compellantur. Eorundem delectorum potestatis quoque sit, si id ex usu Reip, esse putabunt, alterum conventus diem in Smallingeraeo coenobio dicere. Ad eum ituris, domumque redituris tutus commeatus praestetur: Quod si finito decennio non placuerit haec pacta prorogare, aut nova alia inire, foedera tamen superiora & pax nihilominus rata serventur. Anno ab hoc altero, qui fuit M. cccc. lxxix, Arnoldus Lous, quem dixi, ab Imperatore legatus in Frisiam venit cum amplâ potestate, & re infectâ ob quam venerat, discessurus Groninganos sibi substituit, procurandamque regionem inter Lavicam & Flevum ipsis commendavit: firmul promisit, si ad hanc rem ampliore mandato & literis à Caesare se opus habere putarent, ista sese confecturum transmissurumque quamprimum, idque sine sollicitatione ac monito ipsorum, sponte & studio suo: iussitque pro ea, quam habebat potestate, ut delegatum munus & curam seriò & cum fide in se reciperent & gererent. Atque ita ad alia pro Cæsare expediunda, ab his Viennam in aulam abiit. Illic, ex sententia confecto negotio, reversus cum collega Steinbergio in Frisiam anno M. CCCC. LXXXI. inchoante, ( ardebat quippe negotii studio ) diploma secum tulit amplifsimum in commodum ac honorem civitatis, & cum hoc fidei & mandati literas ad senatum, aliasque item ad omnes Translavicanæ regionis Ordines. In diplomate sic scriptum fuit: Oftergoam Westergoamque, & quæ cum his cohærent trans Lavicam fl. sine controversia Imperatoris ac Imperii esse: & has propterea quod procul dissitæ à sede Imperatoris sint, nec ab eo absente curari bene possint, tumultibus atque aliis factionum malis perpetuò premi atterique, idcirco Imperatorem non precibus cujusquam, non ulla alia re, sed solo ipsarum regionum commodo permotum, sponte suâ, re bene consideratâ Consulibus senatuique Groningano optimè de Rep. communi meritis, & vicinia ipsa ad rem opportunis gubernandas eas tradere, munusque illud, quod POTESTATEM vocant, perpetuum tribuere cum omnibus, quæ muneri cohærent cohærent: & velle, ut hoc ipsum decretum suum sit constans & irrevocabile etiam apud posteros: mandare vero, ut senatus commissas hasce regiones cum fide tueatur, regat, pacatas servet: adhæc jubere quoque, Ut QUI IN CONSULATU AUT SENATU IAM SUNT, QUIVE POST IN EUM LEGITIME LEGENTUR, IN EQUESTRI ORDINE OMNES CENSEANTUR: pecuniæ quoque aureæ argenteæque feriundæ jus & potestatem senatui eidem facere: Pro his poscere vicissim, ex assignatà hac provinciâ ut X millia aureorum Rhenensium tributum quotannis sibi pendant: In hunc finem Joannem Steinbergium & Arnoldum Loïm jurecunsultos legatos in Frisiam jam mittere, qui cingulo Equestri Consules & senatores pro more induant, ac reliquis ejus ordinis insignibus ornent, ornatosque statim in possessionem potestatis istius in regionibus Transflavicanæ Frisiæ immittant, omnesque earum regionum ordines jubeant, senatui huic velut Imperatoris legato perpetuo, justa ac legitima edicenti, statutaque promulganti parere, nonsecus ac ipse ea ediceret & promulgaret Imperator. Pœnaque contumacibus & huic decreto obsistentibus denunciata. Signatum diploma anno M. CCCC. LXXX, die XII Calend. Decemb. In edicto ad ordines in his regionibus, præter oppida Doccumum, Leoardiam, Franekeram, Bolsuerdiam, Snecam, Worcumum, longus virorum præcipuæ nobilitatis catalogus nominatim est expressus, mandatumque omnibus, uti senatui Groningano munus illud pro Imperatore gerenti parerent, ejusque edictis & statutis obsequerentur, gravibus propositis pœnis secus facientibus. Id scriptum quatriduo post, ad diem VIII Calend. Decembr. Et hæc quidem monstrata senatui a legatis modo nominatis, legendique copia facta. Sed quod pecuniam in loco negligere senatus nesciret, qui Cæsarem nimis care æstimare honorem & potestatem putaret, nec existimaret, tantum se pecuniæ ex censu regionum conficere posse, crederetque summam in re difficultatem fore, nil horum est effectum. Quamobrem literæ fidei quidem ad senatum scriptæ a Cæsare in archivis Reip. hujus manserunt: sed diplomata cum edicto in aulam sunt a legâris relata ; ubi etiam nunc inter publica Imperii acta & monumenta servantur. Lous de Cislavicanis expediundum negotium in se denuò recepit, atque ita Frisiâ cum collegâ excessit. Eaque ultima ejus in rebus Frisicis mentio. Senatûs abjectus hac in re animus variè acceptus à posteris, velut haud scitè opportuneque usus aulâ pecuniæ egenâ & cupidâ. Anno deinde M. cccc. lxxxi. qui Loi discessum proximè secutus est, Octobri mense Westergoi frequentes seditionum ac bellorum civilium formidine in hanc sententiam cum Groninganis pepigère : Ne Westergoi impedirent eos, si qui sponte sua, sine vi in Ostergoâ vellent se fadere[?] jungere cum Groninganis, nec eorum se rebus miscerent : Groningani contra nullos invitos sub foedus suum traherent, aut rebus novis illic studerent : Westergoa etiam rebus abstineren t : ordinibus his sociis injurii non essent : pax coleretur integra & perpetua.
units.tr: If the appellant does not pursue the suit at the next assembly, or at least at the one after it, he shall not only lose the case but also pay a fine of five marks. The exception is if the judge who gave the sentence does not himself attend the assembly: in that case the appellant is released from the penalty, and the judge who stayed away pays it. The judge and the appellant shall each deposit five marks with the assembly, and the one who loses forfeits his deposit, which the winner shall recover. The covenant was sealed on the Wednesday after Pentecost in the year 1461. Six years later, the Collumers and their neighbours, long troubled by seditions and grievously afflicted, and seeing no other remedy, begged the Groningers with many earnest entreaties to admit them into the covenant. Once consent was obtained, a covenant was made for thirty years. Its terms were these: The city and the Collumers and the others shall jointly provide a strong and suitable house, in which, as in a citadel, a prefect appointed by the city shall reside for the next six years. For this prefect's salary, money shall be contributed each year by the whole countryside, head by head: some shall pay a gold shield, others a half-shield, in two instalments. He himself shall be a help to all against violence and wrong. At the prefect's request the people shall build the ramparts, ditches, and other fortifications. After six years the city and the allies shall consider whether a garrison is needed for longer, and what they then decide shall stand. Criminal trials shall be conducted according to the laws revised at Groningen in the last century. No one shall take part in factions, riots, or other disturbances, even outside the region, nor allow his people to do so. Against armed violence the allies shall give one another mutual aid. Disturbers of the peace shall pay a heavy fine of a thousand gold shields, or suffer capital punishment if someone cannot pay the fine. All violence shall cease; disputes shall be settled not by arms but by judgment, and crimes shall be severely punished. The payment of debts shall be arranged. In civil disputes, appeal shall be made to the urban judges, as is customary among others who have a covenant with the city. Those who did not consent to send envoys to the senate, in the territory of Collum and its neighbourhood, in which those named first are not included in this covenant. The covenant shall stand for thirty years. It was sealed in the year 1467, the day after the Nones of September. Two prefects, Hillebrand Brand and Sibrand Ulverdi, were sent into the Collum territory, since this seemed expedient at the start. Thus peace was secured there, and in the following year a house was built for the prefect. After this, when quarrels and disturbances grew more frequent again in Oostergo, and the flame spread to Westergo too, and the hatred of factions kindled everywhere, and many held grudges against the city of Groningen out of envy and fear, lest some greater evil come of it, at last in the year 1477, through the zeal of wise and good men, all of Westergo and Oostergo agreed to a ten-year covenant with the city of Groningen. Its substance was this: What was made by the whole Frisian nation at Groningen in the year 1422 shall stand, saving the recent Collum covenant. For this decade the Groningers may not bind any other part of Oostergo or Westergo to such a covenant, nor subject it to their own praetorian power. An assembly shall be held every year, alternately at Groningen and at Leeuwarden, to which five wise men from each side shall be sent. To these ten an eleventh shall be added, whom five Groningers shall choose from Oostergo or Westergo when the assembly is held at Leeuwarden; and five Transflavians, from the town or territory of Groningen, when that assembly is held at Groningen. It shall be their judgment to hear, debate, and decide all public and private cases that come into dispute. Whatever they decide shall be considered binding by all. Within the fixed time it shall be carried out by those in whose territory the condemned man resides, or the fine shall be exacted from them themselves; the obstinate, if there are any, shall be compelled by united force to obey. It shall also be within the power of these chosen men, if they judge it useful to the commonwealth, to appoint another day for an assembly at the monastery of Smallingerland. Those going to it and returning home shall be granted safe passage. But if, when the decade ends, it is not agreed to extend these pacts or to make new ones, the earlier covenants and the peace shall nevertheless be kept in force. In the following year, 1479, Arnold Lous, whom I have mentioned, came to Friesland as envoy of the Emperor with full authority. Having done nothing of what he had come for, and about to depart, he put the Groningers in his place and commended to them the care of the region between the Lauwers and the Vlie. At the same time he promised that if they judged they needed a fuller mandate and letters from Caesar for this business, he would himself see to it and send them as soon as possible, and this without their urging or reminder, of his own accord and eagerness. He also ordered them, by the authority he held, to take up and carry out seriously and faithfully the office and charge entrusted to them. And so he went off to the court at Vienna to arrange other matters on Caesar's behalf. There, once the business was concluded to his satisfaction, he returned to Friesland with his colleague Steinberg in the year 1481, at its beginning (for he was eager for the affair), and brought with him a very ample diploma for the advantage and honour of the city, and with it letters of authority to the senate, and likewise to all the orders of the Transflavian region. The diploma was written thus: That Oostergo and Westergo, and the lands that adjoin them beyond the Lauwers, belong without dispute to the Emperor and the Empire; and since these are far distant from the Emperor's seat and cannot be well cared for in his absence, they are constantly oppressed and worn down by tumults and other evils of faction; therefore the Emperor, moved not by anyone's entreaty, nor by any other cause, but solely by the advantage of these lands, of his own accord, having considered the matter well, hands these lands over to the consuls and senate of Groningen, who have deserved very well of the common commonwealth, and to whom the neighbourhood itself is suitable for governing them; and he grants in perpetuity that office which they call POWER, with all the things that belong to the office; and he wills that this very decree of his shall be firm and irrevocable even among posterity. He commands, moreover, that the senate faithfully protect, rule, and keep in peace the regions committed to it. He also orders the following: That THOSE WHO ARE NOW IN THE CONSULATE OR SENATE, AND THOSE WHO SHALL HEREAFTER BE LAWFULLY ELECTED TO IT, ARE ALL TO BE COUNTED AMONG THE ORDER OF KNIGHTS. He also grants to the same senate the right and power of striking gold and silver coin. In return it may demand that the province assigned to it pay him ten thousand Rhenish gold guilders as tribute each year. For this purpose he is now sending to Friesland the jurists Johann Steinberg and Arnold Lous as envoys, who shall gird the consuls and senators with the knightly belt according to custom, adorn them with the other insignia of that order, and at once put them in possession of this power in the regions of Transflavian Friesland; and they shall order all the orders of those regions to obey this senate, as the perpetual legate of the Emperor, in whatever it lawfully decrees, and to observe what it proclaims, just as if the Emperor himself decreed and proclaimed it. And a penalty is announced for the obstinate and for those who resist this decree. The diploma was sealed in the year 1480, on the twelfth day before the December Kalends. The edict addressed to the orders in these regions, besides the towns of Dokkum, Leeuwarden, Franeker, Bolsward, Sneek, and Workum, named at length a long catalogue of men of the highest nobility, and ordered all of them to obey the Groningen senate, which acted in the Emperor's place in this office, and to submit to its edicts and statutes, with heavy penalties proposed for those who acted otherwise. This was written four days later, on the eighth day before the December Kalends. And these documents were indeed shown to the senate by the envoys just named, and a copy was made available for reading. But since the senate did not know how to neglect money on the spot, and thought the Emperor valued honour and power too dearly, and did not think it could raise so much money from the assessment of the regions, and believed the sum would be a difficulty in the matter, nothing of this was carried out. Therefore the letters of authority that Caesar wrote to the senate have remained in the archives of this commonwealth; but the diplomas with the edict were brought back to the court by the envoys, where they are still kept among the public acts and records of the Empire. Lous again took upon himself the business concerning the Transflavians, and so left Friesland with his colleague. That is the last mention of him in Frisian affairs. The senate's spurned attitude in this matter was received in various ways by posterity, as if it had used the court, poor in money and eager for it, unwisely and inopportunely. Then in the year 1481, in October, which closely followed Lous's departure, the Westergoers, in great fear of sedition and civil wars, made an agreement with the Groningers to this effect: The Westergoers shall not hinder those who of their own accord, without force, wish to join themselves by treaty in Oostergo with the Groningers, nor shall they meddle in their affairs. The Groningers, on the other hand, shall not draw any unwilling persons under their covenant, nor pursue new projects there. Westergo too shall abstain from such matters; the orders who are allies shall not be wronged; peace shall be kept whole and perpetual.

units.la: Sed ut unda maris sine fluctu, ita populus exlex & ἀναρχ[?] sine motu & turbis esse non potest. Itaque tumultus minores in Ostergoâ primùm, deinde majores in Westergoâ omnia rursum miscuerunt. Inter quos Smalingani, ut quietos se ac tutos sisterent, anno M. cccc.LXXXVI I. fœdus suum, quod cum civitate Groningana habebant, ampliatum auctumque renovarunt. Imprimis addidêre jam de prætore ac judicibus arbitrio Groningensium eligendis quotannis, deque compellendis iisdem ad faciendum officium per Hovetmannos, & de prætorio Hovetmannorum imperio in eum agrum: de arce, si res posceret, illic extruenda, & præfecto[?] Groningano ei imponendo, de ferendis mutuo auxiliis contra contumaces, & domesticos peregrinosque hostes, ex Upsterano fœdere ad verbum descripta. Quadriennio pòst, anno nimirum M. cccc. xc I. cum Reip. mala crebrescerent, & validiora indies fierent, nil penè cuiquam tuti esset factionum exitialium causa, tandem Doccumani cum Dongeranis, & maxima Ostergoæ parte supplices facti Groningannis sunt, & humillimis æque ac pertinacissimis precibus vix demum ab iis impetrarunt, ut fœdus secum percuterent. Id percussum est in annos XV I II, signatumque die xv Calend. Octobr. Perscriptum in eo de pace tenenda, de maleficiis severè puniendis, de auxiliis mutuò ferendis: adhæc, cæteris judicibus in officio sessantibus Groninganis ut liceret criminis reum delatum abducere ad poenam: cui rei si quis vellet impedimento esse, centum scutatos numos Reip. penderet: ut si pax diffidentibus indicenda esset proposita poena majore x[?] scutatis, indiceretur a Groninganis, poenaque in eorum usum cederet: ut à judicibus Ostergois appellatio esset ad civitatem Groninganam intra diem decimum, deque appellatione cognitio ac judicium esset conventus publici omnium sociorum in urbe Groninga: conventus hujusmodi bis quotannis ibidem agerentur, iisque assiderent aut præ-siderent Hovetmanni oppidani: & hi, licet reliqui, qui adesse debebant, non adessent omnes, tamen cum iis qui adessent, judicia exercerent: reorum mulctas & contumacia poenas more suo per prætorias literas Groninganis exigere ab Ostergois liceret: cædium mulctas dimidias civitas haberet, per mandata prætoria exactas sola in ærarium suum verteret: denique Hovetmannis Groninganis jus esset judices Ostergoos cessantes in officio, ad faciendum officium compellere. Subscripsere fœderi, primùm senatus populusque Doccumanus, antistites cœnobiorum sex, & magnus nobilium virorum numerus, præter vicos & vicanos plurimos, dein plures se paulatim associarunt, demùm universa Ostergoa, exceptis quos factionum studium in diversa agebat, est asscripta : unde fœdus Ostergoum vulgo nuncupatum fuit. Anno postero M. cccc. XCII. cùm tumultus hujus fœderis gratia extitissent, autore potissimùm & concitatore Tiardo Moccama, totaque Sciringiorum factio in Westergoa se commoveret, Leoardii à vi factionis sibi metuentes, ut se magis magisque firmarent, speciali se fœdere & arctiore cum Groninganis junxerunt. Hoc fœdere promisère Senior, Scabini, Senatus reliquus & XIII. viri totius populi nomine, fideles se socios Groningensium suturos in annos XXIIII ex formulâ fœderis Doccumani, ejusque fœderis conditiones omnes servaturòs : præterea permissuros, ut fines[?] civium suorum cum civibus, de quibus appellare superiores judices placet, à Senatu Groningano, temporibus in fœdere Doccumano expressis, recognoscantur: cæteræ lites aut cum peregrinis, aut peregrinorum cum iisdem peregrinis, id est, iis qui Leoardiæ domicilium non habent, ab Ho-vetmannis Groningensibus, & conventu juridico sociorum, ut est in eodem fœdere Doccumano, definiantur. Dein additum, ut Groningani præfectum dent Leoardianis, qui vel in oppido, vel in ejus vicinia commodo loco sedem habeat: isque scabini aut senioris locum teneat in senatu oppidano eaque potestate sit, quâ ipse, si adsit, senatus Groninganus,, cujus vicem geret: eidemque præfecto Leoardiani stipendium solvant decennio proximo aureos Rhenanos centenos annuos: interea socii rationem ineant aliam stipendii ejusdem conficiendi, quæ durèt ad fœderis usque finem, sintque Leoardiani ab onere illo centenorum aureorum deinceps liberi. Præfectum hunc si quis ausu temerario occidat, prehensus capite pœnas vicissim pendat, fugâ elapsus omnibus bonis mobilibus & immobilibus exuatur, eaque ad arbitrium senatus in siscum redigantur Groningensium: eadem vero eam si satelles aut minister iussu alterius patret, & ipse & qui iussit, eadem teneantur noxa, idemque supplicium pendant: At si vulnere eundem quis laeserit, poenam vulnerati hominis nobilis duplam solvat. Cetera sunt de obsidibus sex arbitrio Groningensium legendis & in custodia habendis, sicubi contingat foederis huius observationem Leoardiensium vitio claudicare. Signatum celebratumque Leoardiae die VI Iduum Octob. Eodemque tempore magno numero viri nobiles primarum familiarum, qui hactenus foederi Oftergoo se opposuerant tam Westergoi quam Oftergoi, itemque oppida Franekera & Worcumum, cum cohaerentibus praefecturis, cum audissent Groninganos jam Leoardiam ingressos, Leoardiosque foederis feriundi cum his peravidos esse, ipsi quoque re bene deliberata, dimisso armorum consilio, cum Groninganis pepigere in hunc modum: Nefas esset ipsis, turbare Groningenses, & foedus cum iis jam habentes, aut imposterum habituros: nec contra Groninganis liceret miscere se rebus illorum, aut illos illorum; subditos aut regio-nes nes illis invitis sub fœdus suum trahere: quod compertum fuerit eorum aliquem in Groningenses aut horum socios aliquid deliquisse, de eo ad arbitrium quatuor virorum, duorum e Senatu Groningano duorum ex ipsis datorum satisfaciat. Nec multos post dies Snecani, Slotenses, Ilstani; cæterque horum socii factionis Sciringiæ, fœderis hostes, insigni clade ad Barrahusium à fœderatis correpti, cum Boccone Haringæo, factionis principe, ad arbitrium victorum conditiones acceperê. Iurarunt, fœderi Ostergoo non se semet opposituros, nec impedimento iis futuros, si qui deinceps aut Ostergoi aut Westergoi accedere eidem vellent: nullum jus imperiumve in universam Ostergoam, aut ullam ejus partem sibi arrogaturos, ablata reddituros, exules in integrum restituturos, controversa cum Galamæis arbitrio Groningensium submissuros: Groningenses in persequendis injuriis contra Westergoos hac pactione non comprehensos non impediturosː ē sociis in has leges peccanti nemini patrocinaturos detrimenta impendia, molestias belli Groninganis & Ostergois XVII millibus aureorum Rhenensium& quingentis spatio ix mensium ternis pensionibus fartaros. Denique alia obligandæ fidei vincula gravia & aspera adjuncta : quæ in Historiâ expono. Tùm consternatis totius factionis adversæ animis, quotquot ejus in Oftergoâ supererant viri nobiles, quos hactenus pertinacia non siverat accedere, eidem fœderi Oftergoo accesserunt.In hoc rerum statu, cùm omnia ad ampliandos fœderis hujusce fines spectare viderentur, venit in Frifiam legatus Cæsaris Friderici O T T O L A NG I U S canonicus Moguntinus, ut Frifiorum dissidia componeret. Cujus adventu respirantes Sciringii, (horum enim precibus data legati missio erat) animos rursum extulêre turbasque dedêre fœderatis. Nec multò post è vitâ decessit Fridericus I I I Imperator, ad quem reverterat legatus, cætera ad pacandam Frifiam, uti ferebat, procuraturus. Idem verò anno sequente, nomine Maximiliani Regis, qui patri successerat, in Frifiam rediit, mandata secum ferens de Ephoro in Frifiâ, quem P O T E S T AT E M dicere mos erat, designando, &c simul diploma de libertate gentis. Sed &c civitas Groningana, quæ suos quoque homines unà cum sociis legaverat ad eundem Regem, amplissimum diploma ab eo impetravit, quo fœdus Ostergoum utraque petente parte solenniter confirmatum fuit, præsentibus in aulâ, & nequicquam contra nitentibus Sciringiis. Id diploma datum Campoduni die XXIII[?] Maii: eoque comprehensi quoque illi, qui post perculsum fœdus primum eidem deinde accesserant. At litteræ RegisCamstræo datæ, viro nobili, in aulâ noto, Regique grato, dissensionem peperêre: dissensio tumultus dedit : per eos istuc deducta res, ut Bolsuerdia, Worcumum, Stavera, Hindelopa, & maxima nobilitatis Westergoae, maxima item plebis rusicae pars foedus novum cum Groninganis, foederi Ostergoo similimum, percusserint, denique paulo post tota pene Westergoa, exceptâ FRANEKERA cum conjuratis viris nobilibus, in Grogensium ac sociorum potestatem venerit: quod factum anno Christi M. cccc. XCVI.
units.tr: But just as the sea cannot be without waves, so a lawless people, without any ἀναρχία [anarchy], cannot be without movement and disturbances. Thus, first in Ostergoa smaller uprisings and then in Westergoa greater ones threw everything into confusion again. Amid these, the Smalingers, in order to present themselves as quiet and safe, renewed and enlarged in the year 1486 the covenant they had with the city of Groningen. Above all they added: that the praetor and judges were to be chosen each year at the discretion of the Groningers; that they were to be compelled to perform their duty through the Hovetmanni; that the praetorian authority of the Hovetmanni extended over that territory; that a fortress was to be built there if circumstances required it, and a Groningen prefect was to be placed over it; that they were to bring mutual aid against the disobedient and against domestic and foreign enemies, the wording being copied from the covenant of Upstera. Four years later, namely in the year 1491, when the evils of the commonwealth were multiplying and growing stronger day by day, and almost no one was safe because of the destructive factions, the Dokkumers, together with the Dongeraners and the greater part of Ostergoa, at last became suppliants before the Groningers, and with the most humble yet most stubborn prayers they finally obtained from them that they would make a covenant with them. It was made for fifteen years and sealed on the fifteenth day before the Kalends of October. In it were set down: concerning the keeping of the peace, the severe punishment of crimes, and the mutual bearing of aid; furthermore, while the other judges were sitting in their office, that it should be lawful for the Groningers to lead away an accused person for punishment; that whoever wished to hinder this should pay one hundred gold shields into the public treasury; that if peace was to be proclaimed to those who were defying it, the penalty, raised to a larger sum of gold shields, should be proclaimed by the Groningers, and the penalty should go to their use; that appeal from the Ostergo judges should lie to the city of Groningen within ten days; and that the hearing and judgement of appeals should belong to a public assembly of all the allies in the city of Groningen. Such assemblies were to be held there twice a year, and the Hovetmanni of the town were to sit in them or preside over them; and although the others who ought to attend did not all attend, they were nevertheless to conduct judgements with those who did attend. It was to be lawful for the Groningers to exact from the Ostergoers, by praetorian letters in their customary way, the fines of guilty persons and the penalties of the contumacious; the city was to have half the fines for homicides, and the part collected through praetorian mandates was to go wholly into its own treasury; and finally the Groningen Hovetmanni were to have the right to compel the Ostergo judges who neglected their office to perform it. To this covenant there subscribed first the senate and people of Dokkum, the heads of six monasteries, and a great number of noblemen, besides many villages and villagers; then more joined themselves gradually, and at last the whole of Ostergoa was enrolled, except those whom the zeal of the factions drove in opposite directions; whence the covenant was commonly called the Ostergo covenant. In the following year, 1492, when disturbances had arisen on account of this covenant, chiefly through the instigation and incitement of Tiard Moccama, and the whole faction of the Schieringers was stirring itself in Westergoa, the Leeuwarders, fearing the violence of the faction against themselves, so that they might strengthen themselves more and more, joined themselves in a special and closer covenant with the Groningers. In this covenant the Senior, the Scabini, the remaining senate and the Thirteen men promised in the name of the whole people that they would be faithful allies of the Groningers for twenty-four years, following the form of the Dokkum covenant, and would keep all the terms of that covenant; moreover they would allow that the disputes of their citizens with those citizens whose cases the higher judges think fit to be appealed, be examined by the Groningen senate at the times expressed in the Dokkum covenant. Other suits, either with outsiders or of outsiders with those same outsiders, that is, with those who do not have a domicile at Leeuwarden, were to be settled by the Groningen Hovetmanni and the juridical assembly of the allies, as is in that same Dokkum covenant. Then it was added that the Groningers would give the Leeuwarders a prefect, who should have his seat in a convenient place either in the town or in its neighbourhood; he was to hold the place of a scabinus or senior in the town senate and have the same power that the Groningen senate would have, if it were present, whose place he would take; and the Leeuwarders were to pay this same prefect a salary of one hundred Rhenish gold coins a year for the next ten years; meanwhile the allies were to devise another way of raising that same salary, which would last until the end of the covenant, and the Leeuwarders would then be free from that burden of one hundred gold coins. If anyone should rashly kill this prefect, when caught he would pay the penalty in turn with his head; if he escaped by flight he would be stripped of all his movable and immovable goods, and these would be turned into the Groningen treasury at the discretion of the senate. If, however, a henchman or servant committed the same deed at another's command, both he and the one who gave the command would be held to the same liability and pay the same punishment. But if anyone wounded him, he should pay double the penalty for wounding a nobleman. The rest concerns six hostages, to be chosen at the discretion of the Groningers and kept in custody, if it should happen that the observance of this covenant limped through the fault of the Leeuwarders. Signed and celebrated at Leeuwarden on the sixth day before the Ides of October. At the same time a large number of noblemen of the chief families, who until then had opposed the Ostergo covenant, both Westergoers and Ostergoers, and likewise the towns of Franeker and Workum with their dependent districts, when they heard that the Groningers had now entered Leeuwarden and that the Leeuwarders were eager to make a covenant with them, themselves also, having deliberated well, laid aside the plan of arms and agreed with the Groningers in this manner: it would be wrong for them to disturb the Groningers, and those who already had or would hereafter have a covenant with them; nor should it be lawful for the Groningers to meddle in their affairs, or for them to draw the Groningers' subjects or regions under their covenant against the Groningers' will; if it should be discovered that any of their men had done wrong to the Groningers or their allies, he would make satisfaction for it at the discretion of four men, two chosen from the Groningen senate and two from their own side. Not many days later the Snekers, the Slotenses, the Ilstani, and the other allies of the Schieringer faction, enemies of the covenant, were overtaken by the covenanters in a notable defeat at Barrahusium, and with Bocco Haringa, the leader of the faction, they accepted terms at the discretion of the victors. They swore that they would not oppose the Ostergo covenant, nor would they hinder those who afterwards wished to join it, whether Ostergoers or Westergoers; that they would claim no right or dominion over all of Ostergoa or any part of it for themselves; that they would return what had been taken, restore the exiles to their full rights, and submit the disputes with the Galamers to the decision of the Groningers; that the Groningers would not be hindered in pursuing injuries against the Westergoers, which were not included in this agreement; and that they would defend no one of the allies who transgressed these laws. For losses, expenses and the troubles of war they would pay the Groningers and the Ostergoers seventeen thousand Rhenish gold coins and five hundred more, in three instalments over the space of nine months. Finally there were other heavy and harsh bonds of binding faith added, which I set out in the History. Then, with the minds of the whole opposing faction cast down, all the noblemen of Ostergoa who remained of that faction, whom obstinacy had until then not allowed to come over, joined the same Ostergo covenant. In this state of affairs, when everything seemed to aim at enlarging the limits of this covenant, there came into Friesland the legate of Emperor Frederick, Otto Lang, canon of Mainz, to settle the quarrels of the Frisians. At his arrival the Schieringers, who were breathing again (for the sending of the legate had been granted at their prayers), raised their spirits once more and gave trouble to the covenanters. Not long after, Emperor Frederick III died, to whom the legate had returned, intending to take care of the rest for pacifying Friesland, as he reported. In the following year, however, in the name of King Maximilian, who had succeeded his father, the legate returned to Friesland, bringing with him instructions concerning the appointment in Friesland of an Ephorus, whom it was customary to call the Potestas, and at the same time a charter about the liberty of the people. But the city of Groningen, which had also sent its own men together with its allies to the same King, obtained from him a very ample charter, by which the Ostergo covenant was solemnly confirmed at the request of both parties, the Schieringers being present at court and vainly struggling against it. This charter was given at Kampen on the twenty-third day of May, and in it were included also those who after the first covenant had been struck down had joined it afterwards. But a letter of the King given to Camstra, a nobleman known at court and pleasing to the King, produced disagreement; the disagreement gave rise to tumult; through them the matter was brought to such a point that Bolsward, Workum, Stavoren, Hindeloopen, and the greatest part of the nobility of Westergoa, and likewise the greatest part of the rustic commons, concluded a new covenant with the Groningers, very like the Ostergo covenant; and finally, a little later, almost the whole of Westergoa, except Franeker with the conspiring noblemen, came into the power of the Groningers and their allies. This happened in the year of Christ 1496.

units.la: DE FOEDE- RIBUS PA- CTISQUE PER SAXONES TUR- BATIS.
units.tr: On Treaties and Agreements Disturbed by the Saxons

units.la: HOc tempore Maximilianus Rex cum Alberto Saxoniae Duce comparat de Frisia subigenda: Albertus velut Sciringiis auxilio futurus militem in Frisiam mittit: Ei mox alium, dissimulato nomine & consilio suo, submittit Vetcoperorum stipendia facturum, ut regionem attererent, & enervem redderent. Tum cum maturum videretur, fessis pene omnibus diploma in Frisiam missum, quo Frisiae gubernatio Alberto Saxoni sub Potestatis titulo a Maximiliano, & Ordinibus Imperii assignabatur, eaque jubebatur esse perpetua, transfitura in haeredes. Additum tamen, ut belli impendiis refusis, & certa pecuniae summa soluta a Philippo Burgundo Maximiliani filio, gubernatio tota & omne in Frisiam jus ad eundem transiret. Albertus per suos, quos præmiserat, oppressis omnibus Translavicanis, atque à fœdere Groningano vi & aperto bello aversis, inque fidem suam adactis, Groningam quoque & agrum vicinum tentavit. Nam hos quoque ad imperium sibi commissum pertinere ferebat, habebatque pro se interpretem controversiæ Maximilianum. Verùm cùm res per intercessiones & colloquia non procederet, ipse ob filii casum, quem Translavicani Franekeræ obsederant, secundò in Frisiam veniens, liberato filio, & rebus Translavicanis pro tempore constitutis, exercitum cis Lavicam adduxit, nulloque negotio agrum in suam potestatem & fidem redegit. Sed in obsidenda urbe dum hæret, intercedente rursum Georgio Thorenio Equestris dignitatis viro nobili ad hoc à Principibus Germaniæ misso, & cum eo Friderico Badensi episcopo Ultrajectino, colloquium denuò coiit, anno M. D. mense Augusto: in quo colloquio res tandem composita, & bellum diremptum. Conditionum præcipuæ fuere, ut controversiæ inter Albertum & civitatem, de potestate prætoriâ in agrum vicinum cum Hovetmannis, de imperio in Præfecturam veterem, de jure stapulæ rerum ἐπιχωρίων[?], de usu solius cerevisiæ Groninganæ in tabernis ac diversoriis per agrū, de non coquendâ cerevisiâ quæstus causâ in agro, & quæ alia pactis & fœderibus nitebantur, aut more inolita erant, quæ omnia sibi dimitti poscebat Albertus, Cameræ Imperii judicio definienda permitterentur; interea Thorenius nomine keip.[?] Germaniæ sequester rebus[?] illic præesset, agrarios ordines eâ fide, quâ civitati obligati erant, solutos, in fidem suam adigeret, jus æqualiter ex more & legibus regionis aut ipse diceret, aut dici curaret, usque dum Camerâ litem definiret, eo facto, ei omnia singulave rursum traderet, cui Camera addixisset: partes quoque jurarent, judicio Cameræ se obsequuturos: Tantisper verò Groningani manerent in possessione juris stapulæ, nundinarum, ejus quod ad cerevisiam pertinet, & similium aliorum, eo modo, quo fuerat ante litem hanc à Saxone illatam ab ultimâ usque hominum memoriâ: nec licèret butyrum, caseos, equos, boves, vaccas, cœteraqué id genus mercimonia alibi quàm Groningæ in stapulæ loco more solito venundare, venumve proponere, vel in regiones alias prætermitâ Groningâ exportare aut abigere: Excepta modò essent, quæ hujus generis viris nobilibus in prædiis ipsorum provenirent, quibus jus esset pro libitu & commodo suo ea dividere: idemque valeret de Dammonensibus. Exempta quoque stapulæ legi maneret Præfectura vetus, utereturquæ jure ac libertate pristinâ, emeret, venderet cerevisiam coqueret pro libitu, uti solebat, quoad duraret hæc sequestris ratio: Groningani etiam in exigendâ pecuniâ credità & redditibus aliis per agrum retinerent jus & morem solitum, modò ut judex in eo tribunali in urbe esset ipse Thorenius, aut legatus ejus, aliúsve pro eo sequester ab Ordinibus Imperii datus. Atque hæc probata signataque ab utrâque parte, & sigillis quoque duorum intercessorum ad fidem munita: denique pax constituta. Nec multò pòst Albertus jam tum corpo-re ægro Emdam delatus, atque tibi vitâ functus est. Thorenius verò intempestivè Frisiâ evocatus ab Henrico Alberti filio, malis adhuc haud benè positis, quæ in Rep. sociorum hærebant, (erant enim nobilitatis agrariæ animi in civitatem, & hujus vicissim in illam ex injuriis mutuis exacerbati) quibus ipsum se interponere,remediumque adhibere conveniebat, cùm diutiùs etiam quàm par esset emansitaret, occasioni fuit, ut anno proximo in arma rursum sit itum, transactioque neglecta penè evanuerit.
units.tr: At this time Maximilian the King came to an agreement with Albert, Duke of Saxony, about subduing Friesland. Albert, as though he were going to give help to the Sciringians, sent soldiers into Friesland. Soon afterwards he sent another force, under the pretence of paying the Vetcoperi, with his real purpose and plan concealed, so that they might wear the region down and leave it weak. Then, when the time seemed ripe and nearly everyone was exhausted, a charter was sent into Friesland by which the government of Friesland was assigned to Albert of Saxony by Maximilian and the Imperial Estates, with the title of Governor. It was ordered that this should be permanent and pass to his heirs. It was added, however, that once the costs of the war had been repaid and a fixed sum of money paid, the whole government and every right in Friesland would pass to Philip of Burgundy, son of Maximilian. Albert, through men he had sent ahead, overpowered all the people across the Lauwers and forced them, by violence and open war, to turn away from the Groningen alliance and submit to his authority. Then he made an attempt on Groningen itself and the neighbouring land as well. For he claimed that these also belonged to the power committed to him, and he had Maximilian as the interpreter of the dispute on his side. But since matters did not advance through mediation and conferences, Albert himself came into Friesland a second time, because of the capture of his son, whom the men across the Lauwers had besieged at Franeker. Having freed his son and settled affairs among the men across the Lauwers for the time being, he led his army to this side of the Lauwers and brought the land under his power and authority without any trouble. But while he remained besieging the city, another conference was again convened, in August of the year 1500, through the mediation once more of Georg Thoren, a nobleman of knightly rank who had been sent for this purpose by the Princes of Germany, and with him Frederick of Baden, bishop of Utrecht. In this conference the matter was at last settled and the war brought to an end. The chief conditions were these: that the disputes between Albert and the city, concerning the praetorian power over the neighbouring land together with the Hovetmen, concerning authority over the old Prefecture, concerning the staple right of local goods [ἐπιχωρίων], concerning the use of Groningen beer alone in taverns and inns throughout the countryside, concerning the non-brewing of beer for profit in the countryside, and other matters that rested on agreements and treaties or were established by custom, all of which Albert demanded should be dismissed, should be left to be decided by the judgement of the Imperial Chamber. Meanwhile, the war was ended. Thoren, as sequestrator in the name of Germany, was to preside over affairs there, and to bind the rural orders, released from the oath by which they were obliged to the city, to his own allegiance. He was himself, or was to see to it that someone declared law equally according to the custom and laws of the region, until the Chamber settled the suit. When this was done, he would hand over everything, both whole and in parts, to whomever the Chamber should adjudge it. The parties were also to swear that they would obey the judgement of the Chamber.
